channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Russia Sends Official Note to Kazakhstan Over Arrest of Rapper Navai
item.description: Russia's Consulate General in Almaty has sent a diplomatic note to Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry following the two-month arrest of Russian rapper Navai (Navai Bakirov). Russian diplomats requested official explanations regarding the detention of the Russian citizen and offered consular assistance. Navai faces charges related to drug smuggling.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes Working Visit to Baku
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, has concluded his working visit to Azerbaijan. During the visit, he met with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev to discuss strategic partnership and cooperation. Mirziyoyev also attended the CICA summit in Baku, proposing initiatives on Asian trust infrastructure, technological cooperation, and climate resilience. He held separate meetings with leaders from Qatar, Laos, Cambodia, and Vietnam before departing for Tashkent.

item.title: Trump Targets Iran's Energy Sector, Pentagon Prepares Strike Options
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has instructed the military to develop options for striking Iran's energy facilities, according to CNN. The U.S. is reportedly considering a series of intense strikes followed by a withdrawal. Specific timelines and targets are not yet confirmed. Trump previously stated the conflict with Tehran would end soon and aims to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.

item.title: EU, US, and China Adopt Different Approaches to Regulating AI
item.description: The EU, US, and China are implementing distinct strategies for artificial intelligence regulation amidst global pressure to control powerful AI systems. Concerns range from AI-powered cyberattacks to national security threats and the societal impact of AI. The EU favors mandatory rules, the US relies on voluntary commitments and executive orders, while China enforces state-controlled regulation while resisting calls to slow development.

item.title: Almaty Police Register 46 Cases During Nighttime Raid on Minors
item.description: Almaty police conducted nighttime raids to ensure the safety of minors and prevent juvenile delinquency, identifying children without adult supervision. The operation registered 46 violations, including two cases of minors in entertainment venues, 40 cases of children outside after curfew, and one case of underage drinking. Three minors were placed in child support centers. Police emphasized the shared responsibility for child safety.

item.title: Europe Eyes Independent Spaceflight Capability Amid Geopolitical Tensions
item.description: The European Space Agency (ESA) aims to develop independent astronaut launch capabilities, seeking alternatives to reliance on Russia and the US. Record budget commitments and a mandate for non-aggressive security applications support this goal. Geopolitical tensions highlight the need for Europe to control its space access, currently limited to the US, China, and Russia.

item.title: Ecologists Confirm Kazцинk Responsible for Ust-Kamenogorsk Air Pollution
item.description: Environmentalists have officially confirmed that Kazцинk exceeded emission standards, causing air pollution in Ust-Kamenogorsk. Laboratory analysis revealed improper operation of gas treatment facilities. The company faces administrative penalties and has been ordered to immediately repair its equipment. Previously, Kazцинk was fined for releasing 2,800 tons of zinc dust.

item.title: Europe's Agriculture and Solar Energy Vie for Land, Agrivoltaics Offers Solution
item.description: Europe faces a land use conflict between agriculture and solar energy. Agrivoltaics, integrating solar panels with crops, offers a potential solution by protecting harvests and boosting farmer income. While studies suggest significant electricity generation potential, critics worry it distracts from core land use issues. The technology aims for coexistence rather than competition.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Car Recycling Program Launch Delayed, Ministry Clarifies
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources has officially clarified that the car recycling program is not yet operational. Despite rumors, citizens cannot currently submit old vehicles for recycling and receive discount certificates. The ministry stated that an approved order, effective October 25, 2026, outlines the program's legal framework but does not signify its immediate launch.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Vietnam Discuss Further Development of Bilateral Relations
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Vietnam's Vice President Vo Thi Anh Xuan on the sidelines of the CICA summit. They discussed practical aspects of strengthening and expanding mutually beneficial ties, noting dynamic development and regular contacts. Opportunities for joint projects in petrochemicals, electrical engineering, textiles, and agriculture were highlighted, along with regional and international issues.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis Attack Presidential Palace in Aden with Missiles and Drones
item.description: The Houthi movement launched missiles and drones targeting the Maashiq presidential palace in Aden, Yemen. The attack resulted in casualties among security personnel, with reports indicating four deaths and ten injuries. The Yemeni government, temporarily based in Aden, condemned the attack and affirmed its commitment to continue operations from the city.

item.title: Central Asian Leaders Prioritize Trade and Security Cooperation at Baku Summit
item.description: Leaders from Central Asia convened in Baku, Azerbaijan, for the CICA summit, advocating for enhanced transport links and collaborative action on water scarcity. They emphasized that practical cooperation can mitigate political disputes and prevent conflicts. The summit adopted the Baku Declaration, focusing on economic ties, transport, digital connections, and energy security.

item.title: Uzbek Scientists Prepare for Expedition to India to Explore Ibn Sina's Legacy
item.description: Uzbek scientists are planning their first scientific expedition to India in November to study the legacy of Ibn Sina. The Ambassador of India to Uzbekistan and the head of the Ibn Sina Public Foundation discussed preparations and expected outcomes. India expressed full support and readiness to assist.

item.title: Kazakh President Attends Leaders Summit on Biodiversity in Yerevan
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev attended the opening of the Leaders Summit on Biodiversity Issues in Yerevan, held on the sidelines of COP17. The event featured an interactive show highlighting global biodiversity conservation and nature protection efforts. Several heads of state were present.

item.title: Two Foreign Nationals Arrested in Tashkent Region for Attempting to Sell 2.2 kg of Opium
item.description: Two foreign nationals were apprehended in the Tashkent region while attempting to sell 2.18 kg of opium. The State Security Service reported that the men, aged 54 and 50, had illegally smuggled the drugs into the country. They were caught in the act of selling the narcotics for $20,000 to a conditional buyer. Criminal proceedings have been initiated.

item.title: UK Envoy: Afghan Women's Voices Crucial for Country's Future Stability and Prosperity
item.description: Britain's special envoy for Afghanistan, Richard Lindsay, stated that Afghan women's voices are essential for the country's future stability and prosperity. Following meetings with women, civil society representatives, and journalists in Kabul, he reaffirmed the UK's support for women's and girls' rights and full participation. Discussions also covered regional stability, security, and economic development.

item.title: Two railway workers injured in Aqtobe region after gasoline ignites during transfer
item.description: Two workers of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) were hospitalized in the city of Shalkar, Aqtobe region, after gasoline ignited while being transferred between containers. The incident occurred during routine work on October 13. One worker sustained severe burns covering 80% of his body. An investigation into the safety protocols is underway.

item.title: Worker falls five meters during renovation of Atyrau railway station, another injured
item.description: A 42-year-old worker fell approximately five meters during the renovation of the Atyrau railway station, sustaining injuries and requiring hospitalization. Another worker suffered minor injuries and was sent home after medical examination. The renovation project, started in March, is being carried out by 'Zapad Alians Stroy' LLP.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Investigates Taxi Aggregators' Pricing Practices
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee has launched an investigation into taxi aggregators regarding their pricing and potential unfair competition. The probe follows public complaints about surge pricing during peak hours, allegedly due to 'technical issues' with major aggregators. The committee will assess the justification for price hikes and adherence to competition laws.

item.title: President Tokayev Visits Armenia for Biodiversity Summit
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrived in Yerevan, Armenia, to participate in the Leaders' Summit on Biodiversity within the framework of COP17, following an invitation from Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. He was welcomed by official representatives of the Armenian government at the airport.

item.title: Police Pursue and Stop Chinese National Driving Under Influence in Almaty
item.description: Almaty police pursued a car with Chinese license plates after the driver ignored demands to stop. The vehicle was eventually blocked, and the driver, a Chinese national, was found to be moderately intoxicated. The case has been sent to court for drunk driving charges.

item.title: Taliban Spokesperson Criticizes UNAMA Report for Negative Portrayal
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid accused the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) of engaging in propaganda and negatively portraying the group. He stated that detentions by the Ministry for the Propagation of Virtue and Prevention of Vice were in accordance with Taliban laws, not arbitrary as UNAMA reported. UNAMA documented 443 arbitrary detentions and 97 mistreatment cases.

item.title: Individuals Apprehended Attempting to Smuggle 15 kg of Narcotics in Tashkent Region
item.description: Authorities in the Tashkent region have arrested individuals attempting to smuggle 15 kilograms of narcotics. During two rapid operations, 13 kg of hashish and 2 kg of opium were seized. The suspects have been detained, and criminal proceedings have been initiated against them.

item.title: Astana Car Dealership Manager Sentenced to Six Years for Fraudulent Sales
item.description: A sales manager at an Astana car dealership has been sentenced to six years in prison for illegally selling eight vehicles and taking money for three others without delivering them. The court found the manager falsified documents to facilitate the sale of eight JAC J7 cars worth 53.1 million tenge, pocketing the proceeds. He also took 16.5 million tenge for three additional cars.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives in Yerevan for Biodiversity Summit
item.description: Following a working visit to Baku, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Yerevan to participate in the COP17 biodiversity summit. He was invited by Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. Tokayev previously attended the CICA summit in Baku, where he proposed a preventive diplomacy mechanism and advocated for strengthening Asian security institutions and establishing a water partnership.

item.title: Astana Car Dealership Manager Sentenced for Fraudulent Vehicle Sales
item.description: A car dealership manager in Astana has been sentenced to six years in prison for defrauding customers. He used forged documents to sell eight JAC J7 vehicles worth 53.1 million tenge, pocketing the proceeds. He also took 16.5 million tenge for three other cars he never intended to deliver. The total damage amounted to 69.6 million tenge. The court also banned him from sales-related positions for eight years.

item.title: UNICEF Warns of Rising Malnutrition in Afghanistan, Projecting Over Four Million Children Needing Treatment in 2027
item.description: UNICEF reports a surge in acute malnutrition in Afghanistan, projecting over four million children will require treatment in 2027. The number of provinces with critical malnutrition levels is expected to rise from 10 in 2026 to 14 in 2027. Approximately 1.9 million children may suffer severe acute malnutrition, and nearly three million moderate acute malnutrition. Food poverty, lack of safe water, disease outbreaks, and funding shortages are cited as key factors.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives in Yerevan for Biodiversity Summit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Yerevan, Armenia, at the invitation of Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. President Tokayev will participate in the Summit of Leaders on Biodiversity within COP17. He was met by Armenian government officials upon arrival. Previously, he was on a working visit to Azerbaijan for the 7th CICA summit.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Saudi Arabia May Simplify Visa Procedures to Boost Tourism
item.description: Uzbekistan and Saudi Arabia are considering simplifying visa procedures to increase tourist flow. Discussions also covered expanding direct flights and implementing joint investment projects in the tourism sector. The aim is to enhance bilateral cooperation and facilitate travel between the two nations, fostering greater cultural exchange and economic ties.

item.title: Uzbek Presidential Aide Saida Mirziyoyeva Meets Turkish President, Visits University and Defense Company
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Uzbek presidential administration, met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara. She conveyed greetings from President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and discussed strengthening bilateral ties. Mirziyoyeva also visited Ibn Haldun University and a defense company in Istanbul, expressing interest in their educational methods and youth development approaches. Agreements were made to expand educational exchanges.

item.title: FAO Warns of Worsening Humanitarian Crisis in Afghanistan Due to Migrant Returns and Rising Prices
item.description: The UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reports that Afghanistan's humanitarian crisis is escalating. Factors include the return of over 1.2 million migrants from Iran and Pakistan, increased prices for essential goods due to trade route disruptions, and insufficient humanitarian funding. The approaching winter threatens to exacerbate hunger and malnutrition.

item.title: Afghan Islamic Emirate Urges UNAMA to Base Reports on Factual Information
item.description: Afghanistan's Islamic Emirate, through its deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat, has called on UNAMA to ensure its reports are based on accurate and objective facts. Fitrat criticized UNAMA's latest report for labeling detentions as "arbitrary," asserting they comply with laws, and questioned the omission of the Emirate's achievements.

item.title: Man Sentenced to Life Imprisonment for Abandoning Newborn in Semey
item.description: A man has been sentenced to life imprisonment in Semey for the death of a newborn baby found in a dumpster. The baby's mother, a 20-year-old former police junior sergeant, received a two-year sentence but was released due to an amnesty law. The father was convicted of murdering a minor.

item.title: Houthis Strike Presidential Palace Complex in Yemen, Two Guards Killed
item.description: The Houthi movement launched five missiles at the presidential palace complex in Aden, Yemen, resulting in the deaths of two security guards. The Prime Minister and government members present in the palace were unharmed. The attack occurred at the presidential palace complex in Aden.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan Sign Agreement to Boost Middle Corridor Transport
item.description: Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at developing the Middle Corridor. This initiative seeks to strengthen transport and logistics links, enhance transit efficiency, and fully utilize the route's potential. The agreement includes commitments to ensure sufficient capacity and stable tariffs.

item.title: Tashkent Faces Shortage of 141,000 School Places and 65,000 Kindergarten Spots
item.description: Tashkent is experiencing a significant shortage of educational facilities, with a deficit of 141,000 school places and 65,000 kindergarten spots projected for the 2025/2026 academic year. Authorities plan to build new schools and expand existing ones to address the growing demand.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Turkey clash over new school hijab ban
item.description: Azerbaijan has banned hijabs and other religious attire in state schools, sparking protests and arrests. Critics argue the secularism-based ban infringes on religious freedom and child rights. The government has also reportedly restricted access to social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok, even with VPNs, amid public discontent.

item.title: South Korea elevates Central Asia ties with first presidential summit
item.description: South Korea held its first summit with all five Central Asian presidents, institutionalizing a relationship over 30 years old. The focus was on critical minerals and supply chain security. Seoul seeks diversified supply chains, while Central Asian nations aim for industrial development and skills through foreign investment in their resources.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Artificial Intelligence for Archival Document Expertise from 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce artificial intelligence for the expertise of archival documents starting in 2027. AI will be used for initial document analysis, checking compliance with requirements, and identifying errors. The initiative aims to streamline archival processes and prevent the excessive demand for documents from organizations.

item.title: Former Probation Inspector Faces Trial for Allegedly Driving Wife to Suicide Attempt
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against Behzod Olimov, a former probation inspector in Uzbekistan's Oqdaryo district, accused of driving his wife to a suicide attempt. He faces charges including intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm and threats of violence. The investigation links his alleged abuse to his wife's May 2026 suicide attempt, which resulted in life-threatening injuries.
